I'm a 57-year-old farmer in Quzhou County. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those science papers — I learn by watching and doing. I've farmed for 20 years, and I've got 14 mu of land. There are 8 of us in the house, but my son and his wife work in the factory in Handan, so they're only home for the busy season. My wife, my younger daughter, and I do most of the farm work.

I plant cotton on 8 mu — that's my cash crop. The other 6 mu I do wheat in winter and maize in summer, mostly for our own food and to feed the pigs.

**Cotton:** I plant around April 20th, same as everyone in the village. I use the same seed as last year — I save some from my own crop and buy a bit from Old Wang down the road. Before planting, I spread one big bag of compound fertilizer for every two mu, and about half a bag of phosphate per mu. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July, I topdress with another half bag of urea per mu. I irrigate twice — once at flowering, once when the bolls are growing. Pumping water costs money, so I don't do more unless it's very dry. I spray for insects three or four times; the cotton bollworm can be bad. For picking in September and October, my family does the first round, but I hire women from the village to help with the second and third pickings — there's just too much for us alone.

**Wheat:** I plant in mid-October right after the maize comes out. I use mostly seed I saved from last year, maybe buy a little if I'm short. I plow quick after maize harvest. Before planting I put down compound fertilizer, about one bag for every three mu. Then in March when the wheat turns green, if it looks yellow I spread some urea. I water three times: at green-up, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. I spray herbicide once in spring — the weeds are terrible if you skip it.

**Maize:** This is the rush time. We cut wheat around June 8th-10th, and maize has to go in the same day or next day. I hire the tractor guy with the planter — costs me money but I can't plant fast enough by hand. I put fertilizer down with the planter, about the same amount as for wheat. If July brings rain I might not water, but usually I irrigate once when it gets hot and dry. Maize is easier. We harvest in late September, right when cotton picking is heaviest — September is always a hard month.

This year I'm keeping spending tight because my son says the factory might cut overtime. Fertilizer at the shop went up again, so I'm using maybe a little less than last year, but not too much — I'd rather waste a bit of money than lose half my yield. I need to keep some cash in my pocket for emergencies. I'll be happy if I match last year: about 250 kg of cotton per mu, 380 kg of wheat, and 400-odd kg of maize.
